# Selected source excerpts

These are selected English-language passages from Rowan’s accounts, prepared for this reading draft. They are not the full source records. Some passages are omitted, and a friend’s name is replaced throughout with the bracketed label “[a school friend]”. No translation has been made. The original master records are not included in this copy. All material is fictional.

## Moving-day recollection

**Speaker:** Rowan. **Narrated:** 2026-11-06. **Event:** The move, subsequently corrected to 7 September 2019. **Source:** First-move interview, answer 1. These are separate selected passages, not a continuous quotation; the original tentative event date is omitted in favor of the correction below.

“The chipped yellow mug, oddly. I was moving from my parents' flat to a room above a bakery in Bellwick.”

“We put the mug on the windowsill because there wasn't a table yet.”

## First-evening recollection

**Speaker:** Rowan. **Narrated:** 2026-11-06. **Event:** First evening after the move. **Source:** First-move interview, answer 2. Selected passage; name substituted as labeled above.

“I wasn't regretting moving. I liked having my own key. I just hadn't realized how unfamiliar evening could feel without the kitchen radio from home. [a school friend] had left by then, but texted a photo of an empty bookshelf and said their arms were enjoying retirement.”

## At the bakery window

**Author:** Rowan. **Published:** 2019-09-09. **Event field in the supplied record:** “The Saturday before this post”. **Recording date:** Not supplied. **Source ID:** move-post-01. Selected passages with a name substitution; the break between them marks omitted text.

“Two days after moving, the yellow mug is still on the windowsill. [a school friend] carried the books up two flights on Saturday.”

“The room over the bakery smells like warm flour before I wake up.”

## A table at last

**Author:** Rowan. **Published and event date:** 2019-09-21. **Recording date:** Not supplied. **Source ID:** move-post-02. Full post text apart from the labeled name substitution.

“[a school friend] came back with a folding table borrowed from their aunt. We ate noodles from the saucepan and put the yellow mug in the middle, holding the paper flowers Mum had posted. It is not my table to keep. [a school friend] said their aunt would want it back in winter.”

## The window in winter

**Author:** Rowan. **Published:** 2020-01-12. **Record’s event field:** 2020-01-12 for the room described. The table return is an earlier event, dated precisely in Rowan’s correction below. **Recording date:** Not supplied. **Source ID:** move-post-03. Full post text apart from the labeled name substitution.

“I returned the folding table to [a school friend] in December for their aunt. A small secondhand desk fits beneath the window now. The paper flowers have faded, but I still keep them in the yellow mug. I like the room better in the morning than at night.”

## Date correction

**Speaker:** Rowan. **Narrated:** 2026-11-06. **Events:** Move on 2019-09-07 and table handover on 2019-12-19. **Source:** Later date-correction statement. These are two selected passages, with name substitutions. The calendar wording is reported by Rowan; the calendar itself was not independently inspected.

“I found my calendar entry: ‘7 September 2019 — moved into the room over the bakery, [a school friend] brought the books.’”

“Also, the line in the January post was just shortened: I returned the table to [a school friend] on 19 December 2019, and [a school friend] took it back to their aunt. I remember the date because it was the day before my train trip.”

**Editorial note:** The table’s handover from Rowan to the friend is dated 19 December. The onward handover to the aunt has no separately supplied date.
